calibrated.rule: PREREGISTRATION.md: The neuron, and how its one free constant is set

provenance.neurons: 207 nodes: 180 CNS neurons (paper: 177) and 27 peripheral sensory neurons that appear in the matrices (ATEN1, ATEN2, ATEN3, ATEN4, BTN1, BTN2, BTN3, BTN4, pna, pnb, pnc, pnf, pnh, pns1, pns10, pns11, pns12, pns13, pns2, pns3, pns4, pns5, pns6, pns7, pns9, pnu, pnx). Typed from Figure 3 source data 1, with Figure 1 source data 1 for cells Figure 3's sheet omits. Left out: 16 matrix labels no table types as a neuron (midtail3, pns14, pnw, tail5, 139, 149, 168, 181, 19, 35, 40, 44, 5, 57, 82, 89) and 2 typed but not neurons (107, 177).
provenance.aliases: Cor1-16 = coronet1-16; NeckNL/NeckNR = 165/166 (Figure 3 sides); BPN1/BPN2 = 90/92 by numeric order, ASSUMED -- no table says.
provenance.chemical: Figure 16 source data 1, rows presynaptic; value = cumulative depth of presynaptic contact (um). Count = round(depth / 0.06 um), >= 1: nominal 60 nm section equivalents. 72 pairs were not on the 0.06 grid (section thickness varied); worst rounding 0.50 sections. 1663 kept; 550 cells of the matrix with muscle, basal lamina or a non-neuron left out.
provenance.gap: Figure 16 source data 2 (partners > 0.12 um only), cumulative membrane contact depth in um as gap_w, one entry per pair (both orientations summed). 410 kept; 8 self-contacts and 321 cells with non-neurons left out.
provenance.signs: By cell class from Kourakis et al. 2019 (eLife 8:e44753) through open_animal_stage.signs.transmitter_sign (ACh/Glu excitatory, GABA/Gly inhibitory, both or neither UNKNOWN). Glutamate is excitatory by rule. Classes assigned from a MAJORITY statement, exceptions unidentified: PR-I, pr-AMG RN, AntRN. Every other class (BV intrinsic interneurons, PR-III, coronet, BTN, midtail, PMGN, neck, secondary/PN/pr-cor/pr-BTN relay neurons) has no published transmitter and is UNKNOWN. Result: 61 excitatory, 36 inhibitory, 110 unknown.

AMG.basis: 'the AMGs, with the exception of one cell [AMG5], are GABAergic'

Antenna.basis: 'glutamate is used ... exclusively in sensory neurons (photoreceptors, antenna cells, and epidermal sensory neurons)'

epidermal sensory.basis: VGLUT-expressing epidermal sensory neurons (Kourakis 2019 Fig 2b; Horie et al. 2008b)

Eminens.basis: VGAT reporter expression, agreeing with GAD (Takamura 2010)

MGIN.basis: ventral MG VACHT block (MNs, ddNs, MGINs)

MN.basis: motor neurons are cholinergic (Takamura et al. 2002, 2010)

PR-I.basis: majority: 'the majority of the PR-Is are exclusively glutamatergic with the exception of two ventral cells' (VGAT), not identified

PR-II.basis: all VGAT-positive, a subset co-expressing VGLUT; the paper's circuit model treats PR-II output as inhibitory

prRN.basis: VACHT/AMPAR-positive relay neurons of the PR-I circuit (Fig 5, Fig 9 model); registration alone was evenly mixed

pr-AMG RN.basis: majority: registration predicts 5 of 8 VGAT, 2 VACHT, 1 unresolved; the paper's model treats them as GABAergic

AntRN.basis: majority: registration predicts 8 of 10 AntRNs VGAT-positive

photoreceptor_I.why: Type I photoreceptors (23), annotated Sensory. They drive the larva's directed swimming (phototaxis) through the excitatory PR-I -> prRN -> MGIN pathway (Kourakis 2019): the sense it steers toward a place by. Mapping land gained to it is our design; Ciona has no appetitive chemosense in the connectome to stand in for the fly's sugar.

photoreceptor_II.why: Type II photoreceptors (7), annotated Sensory. They mediate the dimming (shadow) response, an escape behaviour (Salas et al. 2018; Kourakis 2019): the larva's aversive visual channel, standing in for bitter.

coronet.why: Coronet cells (16), annotated Sensory: ciliated cells with bulbous protrusions into the canal and dense-core vesicle synapses, proposed as pressure/ambient-state sensors. Their modality is NOT established; they are used for the slow homeostatic 'reserve' signal because they are the remaining annotated-sensory CNS class that is neither visual nor mechanosensory. The weakest mapping of the four.

rten_mechanosensory.why: Rostral trunk epidermal neurons, Figure 1 classes pna and pnb (pns1-7, 9-13 in the matrix), annotated Sensory and described as 'anterior mechanosensory peripheral neuron'. Body-wall mechanosensation, as the fly's Johnston's organ channel is.

provenance.motor: Figure 1 source data 1 classes annotated 'Motor neuron': MN1-5 left and right and the midtail motor neurons (midtail1, 2, 4, 7): 14 neurons, fewer than 39, so dealt round-robin (numpy default_rng(783); a fresh permutation per module, drawn e, p, w, n; neuron i of it goes to group i mod groups): each neuron in exactly one group per module, groups of 1-2, shared across modules.
provenance.params: Open Fly's constants from Shiu et al. 2024 (fly LIF), unchanged; w_gap 0.0 and calibrated false -- w_syn and w_gap are set later by one fixed rule in the JS brain, not tuned here. Ciona larval neurons have not been shown to spike like the fly's; a LIF neuron is a stated simplification.

validation.cns_neurons_note: Held to +/- 5, not equality: the released tables disagree with each other (Figure 1 lists seven PR-III ids for a class it counts as six, and gives several classes as 'n [m]'), and the CNS set here is every matrix label that Figure 3 or Figure 1 types as a CNS neuron.
validation.paper_counts_not_comparable: The paper counts synapses (6618, of which 1772 neuromuscular) and gap junctions (1206). The released matrices give one cumulative depth per cell pair, so the export has pairs, not synapses; no released table lets the synapse totals be recomputed (Figure 3's per-neuron sums give 5,809 presynaptic sites and 968 gap junctions over the CNS neurons alone). Neuromuscular depth in the matrix: 896.3 um (Figure 4 source data: 435.4 um for synapses > 1 section).
